sentences.en: Back in the 1980s, Keoki Skinner was a reporter with a newspaper called the Arizona Republic.
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪80年代，基奥基·斯金纳曾是《亚利桑那共和报》的一名记者。

sentences.en: He covered the drug trade and the border, and he spent a lot of time in different parts of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他负责报道毒品贸易和边境问题，在墨西哥各地花了很多时间。

sentences.en: But he was getting tired of traveling and of being a stranger in every place he went.
sentences.zh: 但他厌倦了四处奔波，厌倦了在每个地方都做一个局外人。

sentences.en: He wanted to actually settle down in Mexico and to make a life.
sentences.zh: 他想真正在墨西哥定居，过上安稳的生活。

sentences.en: That's when I thought about, well, I'd like to be part of a community in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 就在那时我心想，嗯，我想成为墨西哥社区的一员。

sentences.en: But if I lived here and knew what was going on here, I could probably file some pretty good stories.
sentences.zh: 但如果我住在这里，了解这里发生的事情，我就能写出一些相当不错的报道。

sentences.en: So Keoki moved to Agua Prieta, a town right on the border where he'd done some reporting before.
sentences.zh: 于是基奥基搬到了阿瓜普里耶塔，一个他之前做过报道的边境小镇。

sentences.en: Agua Prieta sits just across the line from Douglas, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 阿瓜普里耶塔就在亚利桑那州道格拉斯市的对面。

sentences.en: The two cities are contiguous, one urban area that spans the border,
sentences.zh: 这两座城市紧密相连，是一个跨越边境的城市区域，

sentences.en: divided by a towering rust-colored metal wall, a steep concrete ditch, a line of concertina wire, and a mesh fence.
sentences.zh: 被一道高耸的铁锈色金属墙、一条陡峭的混凝土沟渠、一排蛇腹形铁丝网和一道网状栅栏隔开。

sentences.en: And Keoki did what he'd set out to do.
sentences.zh: 基奥基做到了他想要做的事。

sentences.en: He settled down and made a life there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里定居，并过上了自己的生活。
那是我们的德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: He built a house, married a Mexican woman, continued mastering the slangy Spanish of northern Mexico,
sentences.zh: 他盖了一栋房子，娶了一位墨西哥妻子，继续精通墨西哥北部那种充满俚语的西班牙语，

sentences.en: and ended up having five kids.

sentences.zh: 阿瓜普里耶塔成了他的家。

sentences.en: And the thing I liked about Agua Prieta, it wasn't tourism-oriented at all.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢阿瓜普里耶塔的一点是，它完全不是以旅游为导向的。

sentences.en: It was a very Mexican community, and I was very intrigued by the town for that reason.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常地道的墨西哥社区，正因如此，我对这个小镇非常着迷。

sentences.en: Keoki ended up scaling back his full-time reporting job so he could open a smoothie shop and juice bar.
sentences.zh: 基奥基最终缩减了他的全职记者工作，以便开一家冰沙店和果汁吧。

sentences.en: What better way to get to know this city than to have a business here, where people will come in and hang out and talk.
sentences.zh: 还有什么比在这里开一家店更好的方式来了解这座城市呢？人们会进来闲逛、聊天。

sentences.en: He could listen and observe and probably pick up a few good ideas for the occasional freelance story that came his way.
sentences.zh: 他可以倾听、观察，并为偶尔接手的自由撰稿工作收集一些好点子。

sentences.en: Which in Spanish, it means like a gossip spot, or there's a ruckus going on, for example, of sirens going down the street.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙语里，它的意思是八卦场所，或者比如街上响起了警笛声，发生了骚乱。

sentences.en: Everybody kind of runs out to see where the cop cars are going.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会跑出来看警车要去哪里。

sentences.en: And that's like, well, where's the mitote?
sentences.zh: 大家会说，嗯，发生什么事了（mitote）？

sentences.en: Kiyoki picked the name because, on occasion, he'd been accused of being a mitotero, meaning a nosy person, someone who pries.
sentences.zh: 基奥基选了这个名字，因为他偶尔会被指责是个“mitotero”，意思是爱管闲事的人，一个窥探者。

sentences.en: He wasn't working as a full-time journalist anymore, but that didn't mean he wasn't a reporter at heart.
sentences.zh: 他不再做全职记者了，但这并不意味着他内心不再是一个记者。

sentences.en: He loved collecting bits and pieces of information and asking questions, figuring out what was really going on.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢收集各种信息并提出问题，弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And so that's how I got the name for my business, and it stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我为我的生意取这个名字的原因，而且它流传了下来。

sentences.en: In fact, to this day, how many years later, I'll run into people like at a gas station, and they'll see me, and they'll yell at me in Spanish,
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到今天，这么多年过去了，我在加油站遇到人们，他们看到我，会用西班牙语对我大喊：

sentences.en: Hey, bueno, mitotero, which means, hey, you know, blonde gossiper.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好啊，爱管闲事的（mitotero），意思是，嘿，你知道的，那个金发八卦男。

sentences.en: They don't know my name, but they know I had the mitote.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道我的名字，但他们知道我开了那家店。

sentences.en: It's kind of perfect, though, because it's also where you first started to see evidence of this big conspiracy that was going on.
sentences.zh: 不过这很完美，因为这也是你第一次开始看到正在发生的巨大阴谋的迹象。

sentences.en: Yeah, there was things going on there that it wasn't hard to start picking up stuff.
sentences.zh: 是的，那里发生了一些事情，不难发现一些线索。

sentences.en: Stuff that would eventually lead Kiyoki to one of the biggest and strangest stories he'd ever cover.
sentences.zh: 这些线索最终将引导基奥基去报道他职业生涯中最重大、最离奇的故事之一。

sentences.en: In other news today, something that one customs agent called something out of James Bond.
sentences.zh: 今日其他新闻，一位海关官员称其为“詹姆斯·邦德电影里的情节”。

sentences.en: The story involved the cocaine trade.
sentences.zh: 这个故事涉及可卡因贸易。

sentences.en: Only last week, another 600 pounds of cocaine were found concealed in a truck.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，又发现了600磅藏在卡车里的可卡因。

sentences.en: He has been the most wanted man in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他一直是墨西哥头号通缉犯。

sentences.en: Marijuana, cocaine, meth, heroin, and murder are all part of his business.
sentences.zh: 大麻、可卡因、冰毒、海洛因和谋杀都是他生意的一部分。

sentences.en: And an incredible feat of engineering and architecture that would change the drug trade forever.
sentences.zh: 还有一项令人难以置信的工程和建筑壮举，将永远改变毒品贸易。

sentences.en: It was 1989 when Kiyoki first started noticing some new customers in the juice shop.
sentences.zh: 那是1989年，基奥基第一次注意到果汁店里来了一些新顾客。

sentences.en: It was guys he hadn't really seen before.
sentences.zh: 那是他以前没怎么见过的人。

sentences.en: They had a certain swagger and attitude.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种特定的傲慢和态度。

sentences.en: And he says they often had bodyguards with them.
sentences.zh: 他说他们身边通常都有保镖。

sentences.en: Which is not typical for an outing to the juice shop.
sentences.zh: 这对于去果汁店买东西来说并不常见。

sentences.en: Kiyoki described them as Sinaloa cowboy types.
sentences.zh: 基奥基形容他们是锡那罗亚牛仔类型的人。

sentences.en: So just when you say these Sinaloa cowboys would come in, like, what do they look like?
sentences.zh: 所以当你提到这些锡那罗亚牛仔进来时，他们看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: The Levi's, the leather vests, the white hats that they wear, pickup trucks with Sinaloa plates.
sentences.zh: 李维斯牛仔裤、皮背心、他们戴的白色帽子，挂着锡那罗亚车牌的皮卡车。

sentences.en: They all feel like they were kind of above the law.
sentences.zh: 他们给人的感觉就像是凌驾于法律之上。

sentences.en: They'd double park out in front of my place and, you know, they didn't give a damn.
sentences.zh: 他们会把车停在我店门口的双排车道上，你知道，他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Everybody just kind of stayed away from them because they knew what was going on, that these guys were in town for some something.
sentences.zh: 每个人都尽量远离他们，因为他们知道发生了什么，知道这些人来镇上是有目的的。

sentences.en: Back in the late 80s, the Sinaloa cartel wasn't quite the sprawling, dominant criminal organization it's become today.
sentences.zh: 在80年代末，锡那罗亚贩毒集团还不是今天这种庞大、占主导地位的犯罪组织。

sentences.en: But it was headed in that direction.
sentences.zh: 但它正朝着那个方向发展。

sentences.en: The cartel controlled a lot of the drug trafficking corridor that ran through the Mexican states of Sinaloa and Sonora,
sentences.zh: 该集团控制了贯穿墨西哥锡那罗亚州和索诺拉州的大部分毒品走私走廊，

sentences.en: then across the border into Arizona and onto big distribution points like Phoenix and Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 然后穿过边境进入亚利桑那州，再到凤凰城和洛杉矶等大型分销点。

sentences.en: Agua Prieta fell right along that corridor.
sentences.zh: 阿瓜普里耶塔正好位于那条走廊上。

sentences.en: Kiyoki suspected that these guys in his juice shop, buying their smoothies with $100 bills, were part of the cartel.
sentences.zh: 基奥基怀疑这些在他果汁店里用100美元钞票买冰沙的人，是贩毒集团的一员。

sentences.en: He began observing them, cautiously, from a distance.
sentences.zh: 他开始谨慎地从远处观察他们。

sentences.en: But he also wasn't above marketing to their sensibilities.
sentences.zh: 但他也很擅长针对他们的喜好进行营销。

sentences.en: And the big thing we hyped with them was, we had drinks that we called AR-15.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们推销的一大卖点是，我们有叫“AR-15”的饮料。

sentences.en: And then we had one, we had an alfalfa drink.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有一种，我们有一种苜蓿饮料。

sentences.en: We hyped it as being real good for hangovers.
sentences.zh: 我们吹嘘它对宿醉特别有效。

sentences.en: So they would come in and drink fresh alfalfa mixed with pineapple or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会进来喝新鲜的苜蓿汁，混合菠萝或其他什么东西。

sentences.en: You know, they bought into my advertising schemes, you know, and that's what they would have.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们相信了我的广告宣传，你知道，这就是他们会点的东西。

sentences.en: This, Kiyoki says, is one of the rules of border towns.
sentences.zh: 基奥基说，这是边境城镇的规则之一。

sentences.en: Even if the theory of trickle-down economics doesn't really hold up in other places, it kind of works here.
sentences.zh: 即使涓滴经济学理论在其他地方站不住脚，在这里却行得通。

sentences.en: When you're dealing with border towns and drug trafficking,
sentences.zh: 当你处理边境城镇和毒品走私问题时，

sentences.en: trickle-down economics is a valid idea because in Mexico, these guys don't hoard the money.
sentences.zh: 涓滴经济学是一个有效的概念，因为在墨西哥，这些人不会囤积钱财。

sentences.en: On stuff like big houses and fancy cars, not to mention bribes to local cops and politicians,
sentences.zh: 花在豪宅和豪车上，更不用说给当地警察和政客的贿赂，

sentences.en: and businesses where the narcos launder their money.
sentences.zh: 以及毒枭用来洗钱的生意上。

sentences.en: In general, Kiyoki says, drug traffickers tend to be pretty flashy.
sentences.zh: 基奥基说，总的来说，毒贩往往非常招摇。

sentences.en: But there was one new guy that stood apart from the Sinaloa Cowboys with their leather vests and high-end boots.
sentences.zh: 但有一个新人与那些穿着皮背心、高档靴子的锡那罗亚牛仔不同。

sentences.en: This guy dressed more like a businessman.
sentences.zh: 这家伙穿得更像个商人。

sentences.en: His name was Francisco Rafael Camarena Macias.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫弗朗西斯科·拉斐尔·卡马雷纳·马西亚斯。
zh_words: 弗朗西斯科·拉斐尔·卡马雷纳·马西亚斯

sentences.en: And one day, he offered Kiyoki his business card and told him a little about what he was doing in town.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他给了基奥基一张名片，并告诉他一些他在镇上做的事情。

sentences.en: Camarena claimed to be a lawyer out of Guadalajara.
sentences.zh: 卡马雷纳自称是来自瓜达拉哈拉的律师。

sentences.en: The story that I got from him when he came into my juice bar at one time was that he was a contractor
sentences.zh: 他有一次来我的果汁吧时告诉我的故事是，他是个承包商，

sentences.en: and he was going to build houses in Agua Prieta.
sentences.zh: 他打算在阿瓜普里耶塔盖房子。

sentences.en: Camarena also told Kiyoki that he was pursuing some business opportunities just across the border
sentences.zh: 卡马雷纳还告诉基奥基，他正在边境对面寻找一些商业机会，

sentences.en: in Agua Prieta's sister city, Douglas, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 就在阿瓜普里耶塔的姐妹城市，亚利桑那州的道格拉斯。

sentences.en: And at that point, I didn't know what the score was.
sentences.zh: 当时我不知道他的底细。

sentences.en: I thought he was pretty legit.
It wasn't yet clear to Kiyoki that Camarena was also in the drug trade.
sentences.zh: 基奥基当时还不清楚卡马雷纳也从事毒品贸易。

sentences.en: And it would take almost a year for that to become apparent to the entire city of Douglas as well.
sentences.zh: 整个道格拉斯市也要过近一年才会发现这一点。

sentences.en: And by then, Camarena had already turned the little town upside down.
sentences.zh: 到那时，卡马雷纳已经把这个小镇搅得天翻地覆了。

sentences.en: About 14,000 people lived here back in 1989 when Camarena first showed up.
sentences.zh: 1989年卡马雷纳刚出现时，这里大约有14000人居住。

sentences.en: It doesn't have a whole lot of attractions.
sentences.zh: 这里没什么太多的景点。

sentences.en: One of the main ones is the Gadsden Hotel,
sentences.zh: 其中主要的一个是加兹登酒店，

sentences.en: which was first built back in the early 1900s
when the area was more of a magnet for cattlemen, ranchers, and mining tycoons.
sentences.zh: 当时这个地区更多是吸引牧牛人、牧场主和矿业大亨的地方。

sentences.en: It has a grand marble lobby and these gorgeous Tiffany-style stained-glass windows.
sentences.zh: 它有一个宏伟的大理石大厅和华丽的蒂芙尼风格彩色玻璃窗。

sentences.en: They depict the surrounding Sonoran Desert with its saguaro cactus,
sentences.zh: 它们描绘了周围索诺兰沙漠的景象，有巨人柱仙人掌、
奥科蒂略和杂酚油灌木。

sentences.en: Today, that desert landscape is heavily surveilled.
sentences.zh: 今天，那片沙漠景观受到严密监控。

sentences.en: A network of towers equipped with cameras and sensors
sentences.zh: 一个配备摄像头和传感器的塔楼网络，

sentences.en: watch the southern border and all of Douglas pretty much 24 hours a day.
sentences.zh: 几乎全天24小时监视着南部边境和整个道格拉斯。

sentences.en: Border Patrol trucks with tinted windows cruise the streets.
sentences.zh: 贴着深色车膜的边境巡逻车在街上巡逻。

sentences.en: There's so much history here because this all started with Mr. Douglas.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多历史，因为这一切都始于道格拉斯先生。

sentences.en: On the north side of town, there's a shop called Douglas Diesel.
sentences.zh: 在城镇北侧，有一家叫“道格拉斯柴油”的店。

sentences.en: It's a big brick warehouse with peeling stucco filled with truck parts.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的砖砌仓库，灰泥剥落，里面堆满了卡车零件。

sentences.en: And it's owned by this guy, Gary James.
sentences.zh: 店主是这个叫加里·詹姆斯的家伙。

sentences.en: Maybe we better just start all over.
sentences.zh: 也许我们最好从头开始。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, what's your name and when were you born?
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先，你叫什么名字，你是什么时候出生的？

sentences.en: Gary grew up in Douglas and has lived here almost all his life.
sentences.zh: 加里在道格拉斯长大，几乎一生都住在这里。

sentences.en: He helps fix and service the semis and trucks that pass through the port of entry,
sentences.zh: 他帮助修理和维护那些经过入境口岸的半挂车和卡车，

sentences.en: hauling clothes, electronics, window blinds, and car parts manufactured in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 这些车运载着在墨西哥制造的服装、电子产品、百叶窗和汽车零件。

sentences.en: About 145,000 personal vehicles and more than 2,000 trucks cross the border every month.
sentences.zh: 每月约有14.5万辆私家车和超过2000辆卡车穿过边境。

sentences.en: So a lot of my business is from Mexico.
sentences.zh: 所以我的很多生意都来自墨西哥。

sentences.en: In fact, I would say probably 80% of my business is from south of the border.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想说我大约80%的生意都来自边境以南。

sentences.en: And Gary says that when your customers are people who work in the cross-border trucking business,
sentences.zh: 加里说，当你的客户是那些从事跨境货运业务的人时，

sentences.en: a certain number of them will have ties to smuggling.
sentences.zh: 他们中一定会有一些人与走私有联系。

sentences.en: When you have a foreign country that butts up to the United States and the drug problem that we have in America,
sentences.zh: 当你有一个与美国接壤的外国，以及我们在美国面临的毒品问题时，

sentences.en: you're going to have these kind of transactions all the time in all kinds of businesses.
sentences.zh: 你会在各种生意中一直遇到这种交易。

sentences.en: And so many a times I know people coming into my shop may not be legit 100%.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候我知道来我店里的人可能不是100%正当的。

sentences.en: So I sell them the parts.
sentences.zh: 所以我把零件卖给他们。

sentences.en: But when Gary first met Rafael Camarena out at a local bar,
sentences.zh: 但当加里第一次在当地一家酒吧见到拉斐尔·卡马雷纳时，

sentences.en: he says he didn't suspect that Camarena was involved in any smuggling.
sentences.zh: 他说他没怀疑卡马雷纳参与了任何走私活动。

sentences.en: I remember him being dressed very well, was very professional,
sentences.zh: 我记得他穿得很得体，非常专业，

sentences.en: never looked like he ever got excited or upset,
sentences.zh: 看起来从不激动或不安，

sentences.en: and never said anything that would make you question who he was.
sentences.zh: 也从没说过任何会让你质疑他身份的话。
卡马雷纳性格外向、善于交际，

sentences.en: and he became friendly with some of Douglas' most prominent citizens.
sentences.zh: 他与道格拉斯一些最杰出的公民成为了朋友。

sentences.en: That included the chief of police and the local justice of the peace who owned a lot of land.
sentences.zh: 其中包括警察局长和拥有大量土地的当地治安官。

sentences.en: Camarena actually bought a plot of that land near an industrial part of the border.
sentences.zh: 卡马雷纳实际上买下了边境工业区附近的一块土地。

sentences.en: And he also bought the local business that sat on it.
sentences.zh: 他还买下了坐落在那里的当地企业。

sentences.en: The business was called Douglas Ready Mix,
sentences.zh: 这家公司叫“道格拉斯预拌混凝土”，

sentences.en: and it sold sand, gravel, and concrete for construction projects.
sentences.zh: 它为建筑项目销售沙子、砾石和混凝土。

sentences.en: Camarena hired Gary to help service his trucks.
sentences.zh: 卡马雷纳雇佣了加里来帮助维修他的卡车。

sentences.en: And so I was seeing Mr. Camarena, at least on a weekly basis.
sentences.zh: 所以我至少每周都能见到卡马雷纳先生。

sentences.en: At least to Gary, Camarena's business appeared to be above board.
sentences.zh: 至少在加里看来，卡马雷纳的生意看起来是合法的。

sentences.en: So the Douglas Ready Mix was actually bidding on federal contracts, city contracts, state contracts,
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯预拌混凝土公司当时实际上是在竞标联邦合同、市政合同和州政府合同，

sentences.en: for all kinds of materials that are needed in road building, bridge building.
